About Me

I'm a resourceful and analytically driven data professional with a Bachelor of Science in Economics and Statistics (Second Class – Upper Division) from the University of Nairobi, currently deepening expertise through Moringa School's intensive Data Science programme.

My analytical foundation was built through rigorous academic training in macroeconomic modelling, statistical inference, econometrics, and quantitative research. Today I combine that with hands-on Python, machine learning, and visualisation expertise to deliver insights that directly shape business strategy.

I currently intern at the Kenya Revenue Authority, analysing revenue datasets and building dashboards that track tax collection performance across regions — collaborating with cross-functional teams to improve reporting accuracy and decision speed.

Alongside data science, I'm pursuing ACCA qualifications at KCA University, reinforcing my financial modelling and accounting acumen. My 15+ Corporate Finance Institute certifications in business valuation, FP&A, and Excel further bridge the gap between data and finance.

01

Aviation Safety Risk Analysis

NTSB Historical Data 1962–2023  ·  Phase 1 Capstone  ·  Moringa School

PythonPandasMatplotlibSeabornEDAData CleaningBusiness Intelligence
+

Business Problem

A company diversifying into commercial aviation lacked domain expertise on aircraft risk. The Head of the New Aviation Division needed a data-driven answer to: which aircraft are safest and most resilient to buy?

Using NTSB accident records spanning 60+ years (1962–2023), the analysis was filtered to commercial operations only, surfacing survivability, manufacturer reliability, and operational resilience metrics.

Cleaning Methodology

  • Removed total write-offs — focused only on survivable incidents (substantial/minor damage)
  • Excluded private operators — commercial/professional flights only
  • Dropped rows with missing registration numbers and standardised date formats
  • Created two analytical subsets: Substantial Damage (safety) and Minor/No Damage (resilience)
  • Extracted aircraft manufacturer from the type string via Python string parsing

Key Findings

  • Cessna 208B Grand Caravan — 55+ substantial-damage accidents with zero fatalities. Top survivability leader by a wide margin.
  • Boeing 737-8AS (WL) — led operational resilience with 18 minor/no-damage incidents. Highest structural durability.
  • Embraer — safest manufacturer: 58 zero-fatality incidents, nearly 3× the next competitor (Raytheon at 20).
  • Risk trend shows a steady decline in commercial incidents over the last 10 years — improving industry safety environment.
  • Airbus A330-243, A320-232, and A320-214 also ranked highly for operational resilience.

Rec 01 — Prioritise High Survivability Models

Acquire the Cessna 208B Grand Caravan as the primary fleet choice. Its zero-fatality record across 55+ substantial-damage events provides the strongest passenger protection profile available in the dataset, minimising liability and reputational risk for a new commercial operator.

Rec 02 — Invest in Operationally Resilient Aircraft

The Boeing 737-8AS (WL), Airbus A330-243, and Airbus A320-232 demonstrate highest structural durability — surviving incidents with only minor damage. This reduces total-loss risk and protects capital in the critical early years of fleet operation.

Rec 03 — Partner with Proven Manufacturers

Limit initial acquisitions to Embraer, Shorts, and Raytheon — manufacturers with the lowest average fatality rates per incident. Aligning with safety-focused engineering partners reduces systemic fleet risk and supports favourable insurance terms and regulatory relationships.

02

Box Office Intelligence — Movie Studio EDA

5 Datasets · 3,359 Films · 2010–2018 · Group 1, Moringa School Data Science Cohort

PythonPandasSeabornSciPyNumPyMulti-Dataset MergeROI Analysis
+

Business Problem

A major company planned to launch a new movie studio with no film production experience and no data-driven greenlight strategy. With production costs running $10M–$300M+, the team needed to know: which genres, budget tiers, and quality standards deliver the best ROI?

Five industry datasets covering 3,359+ films were merged, cleaned, and enriched with engineered profitability and ROI metrics to surface actionable investment strategy.

Data Sources & Cleaning

SourceFilmsPrimary Issue Resolved
Box Office Mojo3,359Mixed string/float foreign_gross
The Numbers5,415Currency strings ($1,234) parsed to float
TMDBGenre dataPipe-delimited genres exploded
Rotten Tomatoes54,432 reviewsAggregated to fresh_pct per film

Engineered Metrics

  • ROI = worldwide_gross / production_budget
  • Profitable flag = worldwide_gross > production_budget
  • Revenue tier = High / Mid / Low gross bands for KDE analysis
  • Budget tier = <$10M, $10–50M, $50–100M, $100–200M, $200–500M

Key Findings

  • Sci-Fi & Fantasy — $81M avg per film. #1 genre. Strong median AND mean.
  • Action & Adventure — $62M avg across 366 films. Best volume-performance balance.
  • Animation — near-zero failure rate. Almost no wide-release animated film lost money.
  • $100M–$200M budget tier — 93.1% profit rate, 2.79× median ROI. Clear sweet spot.
  • Certified Fresh films (RT ≥ 91%) earned +30% more than Rotten titles ($47M vs $36M).
  • PG-13 rating — $57M avg vs $23M for R-rated. Maximum audience breadth.
  • Disney earned 2× nearest rival per film ($417M vs $230M). Model: owned IP + quality.
  • Box office market grew 26% 2010–2018 — fewer but bigger tent-pole releases each year.

Strategic Recommendations — Final Stakeholder Slide
Rec 01 — Lead with Sci-Fi, Action & Animation

These three genres average $56M–$81M per film — 60–180% more than Drama or Comedy. Target PG-13 for maximum audience breadth ($57M avg vs $23M for R-rated). Avoid Drama and Documentary as lead genres. Use Horror micro-budget ($1–5M) as a cash-flow diversification play with strong ROI potential.

Rec 02 — Budget $100M–$200M per Tent-Pole

This tier achieves a 93.1% profit rate with a 2.79× median ROI — meaning a $150M film earns ~$418M worldwide at the median. The $10M–$50M range (66% profit rate) is the worst risk-adjusted tier and should be avoided. Scale to the $200M+ tier (95.1%, 3.43×) as studio infrastructure and IP ownership mature.

Rec 03 — Invest in Quality — Target Certified Fresh

Certified Fresh films earn 30% more revenue ($47M vs $36M avg). Hire directors with strong critical track records for the first three films. Budget $2M–$5M for script development before any production greenlight. Maintain release date flexibility — delaying rather than cutting quality is a measurable competitive advantage.

03

Chicago Traffic Crash Injury Prediction

1,044,747 Crash Records  ·  CPD E-Crash System  ·  Phase 3 ML Capstone  ·  Moringa School

Python Scikit-learn Pandas HistGradientBoosting Feature Engineering ML Pipeline Binary Classification
+

Business Problem

Chicago logs 800,000+ traffic crashes per year through the CPD E-Crash system. Emergency responders currently dispatch resources reactively, with no data-driven severity triage. A missed injury means a delayed ambulance; a false alarm wastes finite EMS capacity.

Using 1,044,747 crash records (2015–present), a binary classification pipeline was built to predict injury vs no-injury from features available at report time — road geometry, weather, lighting, and temporal signals — enabling proactive prioritisation by CDOT, CPD, and EMS.

Engineered Features

FeatureLogicEDA Evidence
IS_NIGHTHour 10 PM–5 AM = 145–55% injury rate vs 22% daytime
IS_WEEKENDSat or Sun = 1Fri–Sat AM = highest-risk block
IS_HIGH_SPEEDSpeed limit ≥ 40 mphInjury density shifts right above 40 mph
ROAD_RISK_SCOREOrdinal: dark + icy surfaceIce nearly doubles injury rate vs dry road

Data & Cleaning

  • 1,044,747 rows × 48 columns loaded from City of Chicago Open Data Portal
  • Dropped 11 post-crash admin columns (data leakage risk) and 7 identifier columns
  • Fixed 7,901 implausible speed-limit records (0 mph or >80 mph) → replaced with median
  • Full Scikit-learn Pipeline with OrdinalEncoder + SimpleImputer + StandardScaler to prevent leakage across CV folds
  • Stratified 70/10/20 train/validation/test split preserving 27.1% injury rate in all sets

Key Findings

  • FIRST_CRASH_TYPE is the dominant predictor — pedestrian/cycling crashes carry 70–90% injury rates vs <20% for rear-end/sideswipe incidents.
  • Early-morning risk spike — Fri/Sat 2–5 AM carries 45–55% injury rate, more than double the midday average of 22–25%.
  • 27.1% class imbalance — a naive model predicting all No-Injury achieves 73% accuracy but catches zero injuries. F1 + Recall used as primary metrics.
  • Final model (Tuned HGB) — AUC 0.80 · Recall 68.9% · F1 0.60 on 30,000 held-out test records — 5,609 injuries correctly flagged.
  • 2.1× operational lift — reviewing only the top 30% of model-scored crash reports captures 63% of all injuries, doubling dispatcher efficiency.

Precision-Recall & Cumulative Gains — 2.1× Lift at Top 30% Scored Crashes
Rec 01 — Auto-Flag Pedestrian & Cycling Crashes for Priority Dispatch

Pedestrian and cycling crashes carry a 70–90% injury rate — more than 4× the rate of rear-end and sideswipe incidents. CPD dispatch systems should automatically escalate these crash types to EMS priority-1 on submission, eliminating the manual assessment lag for the category where injury is most certain.

Rec 02 — Pre-Stage EMS Resources 2–5 AM Near Roads Posted ≥ 40 mph

The Fri–Sat early-morning window (2–5 AM) on roads posted at ≥ 40 mph is the dataset's highest-risk compound condition, consistently carrying 45–55% injury rates — more than double the 22–25% midday average. Pre-positioning ambulances near these corridors during these specific hours will cut response time when injuries are statistically most probable.

Rec 03 — Deploy Model Score as a Triage API in the CPD E-Crash System

The tuned HGB pipeline can be packaged as a real-time REST API and integrated directly into the CPD E-Crash submission workflow. Dispatchers would see a probability score alongside each incoming report, allowing them to sort by predicted severity. Reviewing only the top 30% of scored crashes captures 63% of all injuries — a 2.1× efficiency gain over random prioritisation, achieving more with the same dispatcher capacity.

Rec 04 — Audit Dark Road Segments with Speed Limits ≥ 40 mph

The compound ROAD_RISK_SCORE of 5+ (no street lighting + icy/wet surface on a high-speed corridor) is the highest-risk road-condition profile in the model. CDOT should cross-reference high-scoring crash segments in the database against lighting infrastructure maps to identify corridors where streetlight installation would produce the greatest per-dollar injury reduction — particularly for roads posted at 40 mph or above in areas with documented lighting gaps.

Rec 05 — Run Targeted Road-Safety Campaigns May–September

Summer months (May–September) show a modestly elevated injury density compared to the annual average, driven by increased pedestrian activity, cycling, and recreational travel. CDOT and CPD should concentrate public safety campaigns — speed-awareness messaging, crosswalk visibility upgrades, and cycling corridor improvements — in this seasonal window to address the predictable risk uplift before it materialises in injury statistics.
